leadCallout.small: Take-Two's estimate of GTA VI's worldwide day-one retail sales, through the end of November 19

articles.title: GTA VI sold an estimated 24.6 million copies by the end of launch day, Sensor Tower says
articles.dek: The analytics firm puts Rockstar's first-day haul at roughly $2.36 billion including preorders, about three times GTA V's 2013 opening. Take-Two hasn't confirmed any numbers yet.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI ended its first day on sale with an estimated 24.6 million copies sold, worth around $2.36 billion, according to new figures from analytics firm Sensor Tower. The totals are cumulative and include preorders, and they cover digital sales on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
The number moved quickly through launch day. On Wednesday, before the game unlocked, Sensor Tower's presale estimate stood at about $1.65 billion. A Thursday morning reading reported by USA Today put it at roughly 19.1 million units and $1.84 billion, and by Thursday evening the estimate had climbed past $2.3 billion.
## PlayStation dominates
According to the breakdown reported by GameSpot, PS5 accounts for about 18.4 million copies and $1.77 billion, while Xbox Series X|S accounts for about 6.2 million copies and $588 million. That is close to a three-to-one split in Sony's favor, in line with the preorder pattern Sensor Tower tracked over the summer.
## How it compares
GTA V took about $800 million on its first day in September 2013, so GTA VI's estimated opening is nearly three times larger.
## The caveats
These are third-party estimates, not official sales. Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar have not released a unit or revenue figure, though Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has said official data will be shared soon. The estimates also cover digital console sales, so they aren't a complete count. Earlier this month Zelnick told investors the company wasn't ready to declare victory. The next official word will likely come in a Take-Two announcement or its next earnings report.

articles.title: GTA VI breaks the all-time streaming record for a game launch
articles.dek: Streams Charts tracked a combined peak of more than 6 million concurrent viewers across YouTube, Twitch and Kick, smashing Valorant's 2020 beta record several times over.
facts: Up to 3.29 million, per Insider Gaming
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI's launch wasn't just a sales event. It was the most-watched game launch in streaming history, according to data from analytics firm Streams Charts.
As the game unlocked around the world, starting in New Zealand on November 18, viewers flooded into YouTube, Twitch and Kick. A preliminary Streams Charts snapshot reported by esports.gg showed a combined peak of more than 6.38 million concurrent viewers: about 2.66 million on YouTube, 2.5 million on Twitch and 1.31 million on Kick. Insider Gaming later reported a higher all-time peak of about 7.6 million across the three platforms, with Twitch alone reaching about 3.29 million.
## Records that fell
- The previous game-launch record belonged to Valorant's closed beta in 2020, which peaked at roughly 1.74 million viewers.
- According to Insider Gaming, GTA VI also became the biggest single category in Twitch history, passing League of Legends' 3.11 million peak.
- On Kick, it came in second only to Minecraft.
## Who was watching
Much of the audience came through big creators in Indonesia and Brazil. Windah Basudara drew about 267,000 concurrent viewers on YouTube and alanzoka reached about 245,000 on Twitch, according to esports.gg.
The exact figures differ between snapshots, and Streams Charts calls its early numbers preliminary, so the final peak may move again. Either way, the gap to every previous launch is enormous.

articles.title: Ubisoft cuts 166 jobs at its Montreal and Quebec City studios
articles.dek: The layoffs mainly hit production and support roles tied to cancelled or reworked projects, extending a year of closures and cuts at the Assassin's Creed publisher.
articles.body:
Ubisoft is laying off 166 people across its Montreal and Quebec City operations, two of its largest studios and the main homes of Assassin's Creed. The company confirmed the cuts on November 20.
A Ubisoft spokesperson said the company's production needs are changing and that it is adjusting team sizes to match current production priorities and business needs. According to GamesIndustry.biz, the affected staff are mainly in production and support roles connected to projects that were recently cancelled or significantly changed. PocketGamer.biz says the cuts amount to less than 4% of headcount at the two studios, and reportedly include staff at Vantage Studios, the Tencent-backed subsidiary that runs Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Rainbow Six.
## A long year of cuts
This is far from the first round in 2026:
- Early in the year Ubisoft made what it described as a final round of cuts aimed at about 200 million euros in savings.
- It has since closed Ubisoft Winnipeg, Ubisoft Belgrade and Ubisoft Halifax.
- Its headcount fell by roughly 1,100 between April and September.
- In October it announced plans to close Finnish studio RedLynx and cut 70 jobs at Ubisoft Singapore, and said Rainbow Six Mobile will shut down in January 2027.
The timing is notable. The cuts land a day after the biggest game launch in history, a reminder that blockbuster sales elsewhere haven't stopped the industry's wave of layoffs.

articles.title: Steam Machine 512GB is now in stock, but Valve warns prices may rise
articles.dek: Valve has cleared its reservation queue for the base model and closed the 2TB waitlist, while warning that soaring memory and storage costs could push prices up again.
facts: Expected to last at least a few months
articles.body:
Getting hold of a Steam Machine just got easier, at least for the base model. In an update posted to its Steam hardware community group on November 19, Valve said it has fulfilled every reservation for the 512GB Steam Machine and still has stock left. The 512GB model is now simply available to buy on its Steam store page while supplies last, and it ships right away.
Valve had said in July that it expected to catch up on the reservation queue by the end of 2026. That has now happened for the 512GB version.
## 2TB waitlist closed
The 2TB model is a different story. Valve says it has sent purchase invitations to everyone holding a 2TB reservation, and people already on the waitlist keep their place. But it is no longer taking new signups.
## Prices could climb
The bigger news for anyone still waiting is a warning about cost. Valve says it won't be able to build Steam Machines in the numbers it had planned, citing memory and storage costs that continue to increase at unprecedented levels. The company says it is still producing more units but doesn't yet know how many it can make or at what price, and it expects the situation to continue for at least a few months.
In practice, that means today's price may not last. If you were planning to buy a 512GB Steam Machine, the current stock is the safest bet.

articles.title: Rockstar developers say layoff fears linger even after GTA VI's record launch
articles.dek: A Rockstar animation programmer argues union recognition would give staff a voice as the industry braces for post-launch cuts and AI. The vote runs until November 26.
facts: Largest recognized union in UK games history, if it passes
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI may be the most successful launch the industry has ever seen, but some of the people who made it are still worried about what comes next, according to IGN.
Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte wrote an opinion piece for The Guardian ahead of the studio's union recognition vote. He acknowledges there is no sign that layoffs are actually coming, but argues it's easy to see why developers are nervous. In his telling, game workers have learned to expect heavy overtime before a release and mass redundancies afterward.
## AI and a seat at the table
Uriarte also says Rockstar staff are concerned that AI could devalue their work. Union recognition, he argues, would give employees a formal role in managing those changes alongside the company.
## The vote
The recognition ballot is underway and runs until November 26, according to IGN. If it succeeds, it would create the largest recognized union in UK games history. The vote follows Rockstar's dismissal of dozens of staff earlier, which led to accusations of union busting.
The concerns aren't abstract. On the same day IGN's report ran, Ubisoft announced 166 layoffs at its Canadian studios, part of a year of cuts across the industry. Rockstar itself has not announced any job cuts. We'll report the result of the vote when it's announced.

articles.title: GTA VI reviews are in, and it just tied the highest Metacritic score ever
articles.dek: Rockstar's game opened at 99 on Metacritic when the review embargo lifted, matching Ocarina of Time's 1998 record. Here's what critics loved and what they didn't.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI's review embargo lifted early on Wednesday, November 18, and the game immediately settled at a 99 on Metacritic. That ties The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has sat at the top of the site's all-time chart since 1998.
The sample sizes aren't comparable. Ocarina's 99 comes from a couple of dozen reviews written before online criticism exploded, while GTA VI reached the same number across roughly 147 PS5 reviews, every one of them positive. On OpenCritic it sits at 98, making it the top-rated game on both aggregators. IGN and GameSpot were among the outlets awarding a perfect 10.
## What critics flagged
The praise wasn't unconditional. The lowest score so far, an 80 from Australian outlet ScreenHub, called some stretches epic and others dull and restrictive. The Guardian's review liked the game but found the controls complicated and occasionally unfair. Bloomberg's Jason Schreier felt the story doesn't hit the emotional peaks of Red Dead Redemption 2.
## The money side
Investors noticed. Shares in Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, climbed as much as 8.4% in New York trading on the news.
## What happens next
Launch-day scores often drift as more reviews arrive, and player verdicts after release can look different from critics'. We'll keep an eye on both. GTA VI launches Thursday, November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

articles.title: What time does GTA VI unlock? Launch times by region
articles.dek: GTA VI unlocks at midnight local time on November 19, so New Zealand plays first and the Americas last. In the US, that means 9 PM Pacific tonight.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI doesn't unlock everywhere at once. It goes live at midnight local time on Thursday, November 19, so the release rolls around the globe over most of a day.
## The rollout
Regional PlayStation Store listings, gathered by fan site GTAVice and reported by Digital Foundry, show 15 launch windows across 63 countries:
- New Zealand first, at midnight NZDT, which is 11:00 UTC on Wednesday, November 18.
- Australia next, at midnight AEDT (13:00 UTC on the 18th), then Japan and South Korea at 15:00 UTC.
- Mainland Europe at midnight CET (23:00 UTC on the 18th), then the UK and Ireland at midnight GMT.
- The US and Canada at midnight Eastern Time (05:00 UTC on the 19th).
- Mexico and parts of Central America last, at 06:00 UTC.
## West Coast players get it early
The US listing uses a single nationwide unlock at midnight Eastern, so players on the West Coast can start at 9 PM Pacific on Wednesday night.
## Xbox
The midnight-local-time rule covers both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Xbox's store doesn't publish an exact hour for each country, so Xbox players should plan on midnight local time.
Make sure your pre-load has finished before then. On PS5, you also need system update 14.23 installed first.

articles.title: GTA VI runs at 30fps on every console: resolutions, PS5 Pro extras and the update you need
articles.dek: There's no performance mode in GTA VI. Rockstar says 30fps was always the target on this generation of hardware. Here's how each console renders the game.
articles.body:
If you were hoping for a 60fps option in Grand Theft Auto VI, there isn't one. The game targets 30 frames per second on every console, and Rockstar has said that, given how much it wanted to put into the world, it planned for 30fps on this hardware generation from the start.
## How each console renders it
- PS5 and Xbox Series X: renders at 1440p and upscales to 4K.
- PS5 Pro: uses Sony's PSSR2 upscaler for a similar 4K output, with improved image clarity and ray-traced shadows.
- Xbox Series S: renders at 720p and uses AMD's FSR 4 to reach 1080p.
## Before you play
PS5 owners need system software update 14.23, which Sony released on November 17 and marked as mandatory. Install it before launch night so you're not stuck waiting at midnight.
The download is big: up to 212 GB depending on your console. Boxed copies hold a download code rather than a disc, so you'll need the space either way. Digital pre-loading is already open.
The Standard Edition costs $80. Rockstar's parent Take-Two said last week that pre-orders beat its expectations, and GTA VI has become the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

articles.title: The Game Awards 2026 nominees: GTA VI leads with eight, Ocarina of Time remake in the GOTY race
articles.dek: Six games are up for Game of the Year at the December 10 show, and fan voting is open now.
facts: Control Resonant, Resident Evil Requiem (6 each)
articles.body:
The nominees for The Game Awards 2026 are out, and the Game of the Year shortlist is one of the strongest in years. The show airs on Thursday, December 10.
## Game of the Year nominees
- 007 First Light (IO Interactive)
- Control Resonant (Remedy / Annapurna)
- Grand Theft Auto VI (Rockstar Games)
- Phantom Blade Zero (S-GAME)
- Resident Evil Requiem (Capcom)
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Nintendo)
## Who's leading
GTA VI tops the field with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative and Best Performance. It's an unusual position for a game that isn't even out yet as the nominations land. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem have six each, Phantom Blade Zero has five and 007 First Light has four.
Nintendo's Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 makes the main shortlist and also picks up nods for Best Art Direction and Best Score and Music. It's a rare case of a remake competing for the top prize.
Fan voting is open on The Game Awards website now. We'll cover the show and every winner on the night.

articles.title: Firaxis cuts about a third of its staff as layoffs hit Crystal Dynamics and Netflix Games
articles.dek: The Civilization studio loses around 60 people, per Bloomberg, in a week of cuts across the industry.
facts: About 60 jobs, roughly a third of staff
articles.body:
Launch week for the biggest game of the decade is also a week of job losses elsewhere in the industry.
## Firaxis
Firaxis, the studio behind Civilization and XCOM, has laid off around 60 people, about a third of its workforce, according to Bloomberg. The same reporting says a new XCOM game is in the works. Firaxis is owned by 2K, part of Take-Two, which is about to release GTA VI. The studio has been cut before: there were layoffs in 2023 and again in September 2025, after Civilization VII's slow start.
## Crystal Dynamics
The Tomb Raider developer has let eight more employees go. That's the sixth round of layoffs at the studio since Embracer Group bought it in 2022.
## Netflix Games
Netflix's games division has also made layoffs, though it hasn't said how many. A game director there described it as a restructuring while the team changes how it approaches making games.
We'll update this story as studios share more.

articles.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sells 5.2 million in four days, a Switch 2 record
articles.dek: Nintendo's rebuilt classic is now the fastest-selling game on Switch 2.
articles.body:
Nintendo says The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 sold more than 5.2 million copies worldwide in its first four days. That makes it the fastest-selling game on the console so far.
The remake launched on November 5 as a major modern overhaul of the 1998 Nintendo 64 classic, the same game whose 99 Metacritic score GTA VI tied this week. It's also one of six Game of the Year nominees at The Game Awards 2026.
## Also new on Switch 2
Nintendo had a busy week beyond Zelda. Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy came out on November 12, and the eShop now lets you gift digital games to members of your family group. The second part of Pokémon Pokopia's paid expansion, Dazzling Decorations, arrives December 9.

articles.title: Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames
articles.dek: Xbox confirmed the sequel as part of its 25th anniversary celebrations, nine years after The New Colossus.
articles.body:
B.J. Blazkowicz is coming back. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced on X that Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames, as part of a run of announcements marking Xbox's 25th anniversary. The post showed a photographed page from the game's script.
The Swedish studio followed with its own confirmation: "His reputation precedes him."
## Where it fits
The last mainline game, Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus, came out in 2017. MachineGames spent much of the time since on Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, released in December 2024. The studio's leadership has said before that the modern series was always planned as a trilogy.
Reports say Brian Bloom and Debra Wilson return as B.J. Blazkowicz and Grace Walker. There are no platforms, release window or gameplay yet. Because production has only just started, don't expect a proper reveal for a while.

articles.title: Rockstar's UK staff vote on union recognition during GTA VI launch week
articles.dek: The ballot runs from November 12 to 26. A yes vote would create the largest recognized union in the UK games industry.
articles.body:
While the world waits for GTA VI, the people who made it are voting. Rockstar Games' UK employees have until November 26 to decide whether the company should formally recognize the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union, a ballot that runs right across the game's November 19 launch.
The union says about 1,600 staff can vote. If the vote passes, the union would become the largest recognized union in the UK games industry, with a say on pay, bonuses, overtime, redundancies and policies on generative AI. The vote covers recognition only, not strike action.
## The tribunal
The ballot is separate from an employment tribunal in Glasgow over 31 workers Rockstar fired in October 2025. The IWGB says they were dismissed for union organizing. Rockstar says they were dismissed for gross misconduct. The judge hasn't set a date for a ruling.
We'll report the result when the ballot closes.

articles.title: PlayStation cancels Fairgames, but Haven Studios keeps its staff
articles.dek: The heist shooter revealed in 2023 is dead after a playtest missed internal targets. No one is losing their job.
articles.body:
Sony has cancelled Fairgames, the online heist shooter Haven Studios had been building for PS5 and PC, Bloomberg reported. According to an internal email, a recent playtest fell short of what the team was aiming for.
Unusually for a PlayStation cancellation, nobody is being laid off. Haven will stay open and move into a support role, working with other PlayStation Studios teams while it looks for new projects. Sony hasn't said which games it will help with.
## A troubled project
Fairgames debuted at the PlayStation Showcase in May 2023, pitched as a modern heist game about robbing the super rich. Jade Raymond founded Haven in 2021, Sony bought the studio in 2022, and Raymond left in 2025. It's the latest in a string of live-service projects PlayStation has dropped, following Concord's shutdown and The Last of Us Online's cancellation.

articles.title: The hacker behind the 2022 GTA VI leak pleads guilty
articles.dek: Arion Kurtaj, who posted about 90 clips of an early GTA VI build, admitted the Rockstar breach in a London court three days before launch.
articles.body:
The man who leaked Grand Theft Auto VI to the world four years ago has admitted it. Arion Kurtaj, now 21, pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court on Monday, November 16, to crimes linked to the 2022 hack of Rockstar Games.
Kurtaj was a teenager when he got into Rockstar's internal Slack in September 2022 and posted about 90 clips from an early build of the game online. It was the public's first look at GTA VI, including its playable female lead, Lucia, more than a year before Rockstar's official reveal. He also threatened to release the game's source code.
## A long case
Kurtaj was arrested in 2022. He was linked to the Lapsus$ hacking group, which also hit major tech companies that year. Earlier court proceedings found he wasn't fit to stand trial, and in 2023 he was ordered to stay in a secure hospital. Reports say he carried out part of the Rockstar attack while under police supervision in a hotel, using a hotel television and other borrowed equipment.
Rockstar has said the hack cost it $5 million to recover from, plus thousands of hours of staff time, according to the BBC.
The plea lands days before the game finally launches on November 19.

articles.title: God of War Sons of Sparta comes to PS4 with two free new modes
articles.dek: The 2D Kratos prequel is no longer PS5-only. A free update on both consoles adds a speedrun mode and a brutal one-hit mode.
facts: Mega Cat Studios, Santa Monica Studio
articles.body:
God of War Sons of Sparta, the 2D pixel-art spin-off that Sony shadow-dropped on PS5 in February for the series' 20th anniversary, came to PlayStation 4 on Monday, November 16.
The game follows Kratos as a 13-year-old Spartan soldier, long before his war on the gods. It was developed by Mega Cat Studios with Santa Monica Studio. A PS4 version had been rumored after dataminers spotted a PS4 listing earlier in November, but the new content was a surprise.
## Two new ways to play
A free update for both PS4 and PS5 adds two modes. You choose one when you start a new game in a save slot, and you can't switch later.
- Hermes Mode: a speedrun-focused mode that unlocks after you finish the game.
- Erebus Mode: a punishing challenge where both you and your enemies die in a single hit.
## What's next for Kratos
The main series is further off than planned. Santa Monica Studio recently delayed God of War Laufey from February to May 20, 2027.

articles.title: Xbox turns 25: everything announced, from Wolfenstein 3 to original Xbox games on PC
articles.dek: Microsoft marked the anniversary with new games in production, more classic Xbox titles on PC, fresh Fable gameplay and the $900 Series X25.
facts: Wolfenstein 3, a new id Software game
articles.body:
The original Xbox launched in North America on November 15, 2001, and Microsoft spent the week around its 25th birthday rolling out news.
## New games in the works
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is in production at MachineGames, and that id Software has started a new game directed by Hugo Martin. We have separate stories on both.
## Original Xbox games on PC
Microsoft added 21 original Xbox games to PC through backward compatibility, including Armed and Dangerous, Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge and Fuzion Frenzy. That brings the number of original Xbox games playable on PC to 25. Some classic titles also get achievements for the first time.
## Fable
A new four-minute gameplay video for the Fable reboot, due in 2027, was shown running on PC at its highest graphics settings.
## The Series X25
The limited-edition Xbox Series X25, a translucent "OG green" console modeled on the 2001 machine, went on sale on November 13 for $899.99 in select markets. It comes with a matching controller and a copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved.
Not everyone was impressed. Some fans felt the celebration was light on big console news, especially with so much of it aimed at PC.

articles.title: id Software starts its next game, with Doom's Hugo Martin directing
articles.dek: The Doom studio confirmed a new project across its Texas and Frankfurt teams. It hasn't said what the game is, but reports point to more Doom.
articles.body:
id Software is working on its next game. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the project on November 12 as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary, and the studio confirmed it on X shortly afterwards.
Teams at id's offices in Texas and Frankfurt are building it, and Hugo Martin returns as game director. Martin was creative director on Doom (2016) and Doom Eternal and directed last year's Doom: The Dark Ages. The studio said it will be a while before it's ready to show anything.
## Doom again?
id hasn't said whether it's Doom, Quake or something new. The Verge's Tom Warren reports that it's a Doom project, though that hasn't been confirmed.
The news follows a difficult stretch for the studio, which was hit by Xbox layoffs earlier this year. Martin has pushed back on reports that id was cut too deeply to make big games, saying the team is still roughly the size of the one that made Doom (2016).

articles.title: Witcher 3's new expansion uses AI to keep Geralt's Polish voice consistent
articles.dek: Geralt's Polish actor Jacek Rozenek still records every line. AI adjusts them to match his voice from before a 2019 stroke, with his consent.
facts: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past
articles.body:
CD Projekt Red has confirmed that it is using AI on Geralt's Polish dialogue in Songs of the Past, the surprise new expansion for The Witcher 3, first reported by Game File.
Jacek Rozenek has voiced Geralt in Polish since the first Witcher game in 2007. In 2019 he had a stroke that left him unable to speak for months. He rebuilt his voice through intensive daily training and returned to acting, but it now sounds lower and rougher than it did in the 2015 game.
## How it works
Rozenek still performs every new line himself. CD Projekt worked with Ukrainian company Respeecher, which built a model from his original recordings so the new lines sound like the Geralt Polish players heard in the base game. That lets them sit alongside thousands of older lines without a jarring change. Rozenek agreed to the process.
CD Projekt calls it a special case and says its contracts require an actor's consent for any AI use.
## Not the first time
The studio used Respeecher before, for Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty, where it recreated the Polish voice of Viktor Vektor with the family's consent after actor Miłogost Reczek died in 2021.

articles.title: EU proposes banning paid loot boxes and pay-to-win for minors
articles.dek: The Digital Fairness Act would also force games to show loot box odds and let every player switch paid loot boxes off. Industry groups are pushing back.
facts: Paid loot boxes, pay-to-win and pay-to-progress banned
Odds shown, option to switch loot boxes off
articles.body:
The European Commission has proposed the biggest shake-up of game monetization rules Europe has seen. Its Digital Fairness Act, published on November 11, would replace the EU's 2005 Unfair Commercial Practices Directive with a regulation that applies directly in every member state.
## What it means for games
- Paid loot boxes would be banned for minors outright.
- Pay-to-win and pay-to-progress mechanics would be banned for minors too.
- Every game selling loot boxes would have to list what's inside and the odds of getting each item.
- All players, adults included, would get tools to turn paid loot boxes off.
- Paid virtual currencies would be switched off by default for minors.
The proposal groups loot boxes, wheels of fortune and collectible card packs together, saying they share features with gambling. Consumer Commissioner Michael McGrath called it the most ambitious reform of EU consumer rules in a generation.
## Industry reaction
Video Games Europe, whose members include Sony and Epic, and the European Games Developer Federation warned in a joint statement that the plan would seriously hurt the competitiveness of Europe's games industry. They also objected to treating games rated below PEGI 18 as products aimed at children.
## What happens next
This is a proposal, not a law. The European Parliament and member states still have to agree on it, and the text could change along the way.

articles.title: Switch 2 reaches 26.35 million sold as Nintendo holds its 16.5 million forecast
articles.dek: Hardware sales are down from launch year, but software is up and Nintendo is sticking to its full-year target despite rising chip costs.
articles.body:
Nintendo's results for April to September show Switch 2 settling into its second year. The console sold 2.67 million units in the July–September quarter, bringing its lifetime total to 26.35 million.
First-half hardware sales came to 6.49 million, down 37.4% from a year earlier. That comparison is against the console's launch period, when demand was at its peak. Software is moving the other way: Switch 2 games sold 24.49 million units in the half, up 18.8%.
## Holding the line
Nintendo kept its full-year forecast of 16.5 million Switch 2 consoles for the year ending March 2027. That forecast already allows for around $633 million in extra costs from rising component prices, with memory chips the main pressure.
The original Switch is still selling too. It added 1.27 million units in the half, for a lifetime total of 157.20 million.
The quarter ended before the November 5 launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has since become the fastest-selling Switch 2 game. Its effect will show up in next quarter's numbers.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever launches, Blizzard's long-awaited Classic Plus
articles.dek: A third permanent version of WoW expands vanilla Azeroth with new zones, dungeons and over 1,000 quests. Raids open December 9.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft: Forever, the "Classic Plus" fans have asked for for years, launched worldwide on November 4. It sits alongside modern WoW and WoW Classic as a third permanent version of the game, and it's included with a World of Warcraft subscription, so there's nothing extra to buy.
Forever keeps the look and core rules of the original 2004 game but adds to it: updated visuals and lighting, three new zones, nine new dungeons, more than 1,000 new quests and new race and class combinations such as Gnome Priests, Dwarf Shamans and Undead Paladins. The level cap stays at 60. Blizzard has said Forever is a separate continuity from modern WoW.
## What's coming
- December 9: raids unlock, with Barrow Deeps (10 players), Hyjal Summit (20) and Onyxia's Lair (40).
- A Hardcore version later.
- Spring 2027: two more raids, two dungeons, new quests and areas, a legendary questline and a PvP season refresh.

articles.title: God of War Laufey is delayed three months to May 20, 2027
articles.dek: Santa Monica Studio is pushing Faye's PS5 adventure back from February to give the game more polish.
articles.body:
God of War Laufey won't make its February launch. Santa Monica Studio announced on November 4 that the game is moving from February 16, 2027 to May 20, 2027, a delay of about three months.
In a message posted online, the studio said it wants the extra time for finishing touches and to push the game to its full potential. It promised more updates before the new date.
## About the game
Laufey stars Faye, Kratos's late wife and Atreus's mother, and takes its name from the title she earns, Laufey the Just. It's set in the "Everywhen," an afterlife where gods go after death, and runs alongside the events of God of War (2018) and Ragnarök. It's a PS5 exclusive.
The move also takes the game out of a crowded early-2027 release window. In the meantime, PlayStation fans have the 2D spin-off God of War Sons of Sparta, which just came to PS4 with new modes.

articles.title: GTA VI is out now after preorders reportedly topped $1.65 billion
articles.dek: Rockstar's open-world sequel has unlocked worldwide on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Sensor Tower estimates preorders alone passed $1.65 billion, with about three quarters on PS5.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here. After a wait of more than 13 years since GTA V, Rockstar's return to Vice City has unlocked at midnight local time around the world, rolling west from New Zealand on Wednesday to the Americas overnight.
## The preorder numbers
According to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, as reported by Yahoo Finance, GTA VI took in more than $1.65 billion in preorders before launch. Roughly three quarters of that came from PlayStation 5 players, with the rest on Xbox Series X|S. Take-Two hasn't published its own sales figure yet, so treat the number as an outside estimate.
Circana analyst Mat Piscatella told Yahoo Finance that the only real ceiling on the game is how many PS5 and Xbox Series consoles are out there. That ceiling is lower than it might be: console prices have risen sharply this generation, and Piscatella noted that today's machines cost about $300 more than the PS3 and Xbox 360 did when GTA V launched in 2013, even after adjusting for inflation.
## What it's up against
The bar set by its predecessor is enormous. Take-Two says GTA V has sold around 235 million copies, and it reached $1 billion in retail sales faster than any entertainment release before it. Investors appear optimistic: Take-Two's share price was trading more than 6 percent higher around launch, per Yahoo Finance's market data.
## Before you play
- On PS5, Sony requires system software update 26.07-14.23.00 before the game will run.
- Rockstar has also pushed a day-one title update on PS5, so check for updates if the game won't start.
- The game's online mode isn't part of this launch.
Critics have been near-unanimous: the game sits at 99 on Metacritic. Launch night wasn't entirely smooth, though, after PlayStation Network sign-in problems hit players in the hours beforehand.

articles.title: PlayStation Network outage hits players hours before GTA VI unlocks
articles.dek: Sony acknowledged sign-in and connection problems on Wednesday afternoon as PS5 owners prepared for GTA VI. Service was reportedly back before the US launch, but a second blip followed.
facts: Wednesday, November 18, from about 1 PM ET
Sign-in failures, games and apps not launching
Reported restored by 9:18 PM ET Nov 18
articles.body:
PlayStation Network buckled on Wednesday afternoon, just hours before Grand Theft Auto VI was due to unlock in the US.
## What went wrong
Reports on outage tracker Downdetector started climbing around 1 PM Eastern on November 18, according to Newsweek, and passed 4,000 by mid-afternoon. GV Wire later counted more than 23,000 reports. Most complaints were about signing in to PSN and connecting to its servers, with some players told PlayStation services were busy. Without a working sign-in, the PlayStation Store, party chat and online play can stop working too.
Sony confirmed the problem on its PlayStation Network service status page, warning that players might have trouble launching games, apps or network features and saying it was working on a fix. It hasn't said what caused the outage, and nothing official ties it to GTA VI, though the timing was hard to miss with millions of players finishing preloads.
## Back up, mostly
Sony's status page showed all services running again by 9:18 PM Eastern on Wednesday, according to WION. A shorter disruption was reported after the game went live in the US early Thursday, which Sony's status data later listed as resolved. Downdetector reports also rose for Xbox earlier on Wednesday, but Microsoft's status page showed Xbox services running normally.
## If GTA VI still won't start
- Install PS5 system software 26.07-14.23.00, which Sony says is required to play.
- Check for the latest GTA VI title update from the game's Options menu.
- Check the PlayStation service status page before restarting your console again.

articles.title: Sony wins UK class action over PlayStation Store prices
articles.dek: London's Competition Appeal Tribunal has dismissed a $2.6 billion claim that Sony abused its control of digital game sales on PlayStation with a 30 percent cut.
articles.body:
Sony has defeated a major UK lawsuit that accused it of overcharging PlayStation players for digital games.
## The case
Consumer rights campaigner Alex Neill brought the class action in 2023 on behalf of roughly 8.9 million PlayStation customers in the UK. The claim, valued at about $2.6 billion, argued that Sony's 30 percent commission on digital purchases, combined with its control over PlayStation Store pricing, was an abuse of a dominant position that pushed prices higher than they should be.
## The ruling
According to Game Developer, which credited Video Games Chronicle with the original report, the Competition Appeal Tribunal threw out the case. The tribunal's view, as reported, was that Sony can't hold a monopoly over digital sales while players can still buy physical games instead. It also wasn't convinced that games on the PlayStation Store were priced too high.
That reasoning may not age well. Game Developer notes that PlayStation plans to stop producing physical software in 2028, which would remove the alternative the tribunal leaned on.
## What's next
The UK case won't go further, per Game Developer. Similar challenges to Sony's store fees are under way in Australia, the Netherlands, Portugal and the US, and any of them could still put pressure on the 30 percent cut if they make progress. A win in London would likely have forced Sony to rethink those fees.

articles.title: European game worker unions call for an end to generative AI use where possible
articles.dek: Unions in the UK, Ireland, Spain and Italy have published a joint manifesto arguing that generative AI is costing jobs and making working conditions worse.
facts: 55% of devs see genAI as a negative
articles.body:
A coalition of European game industry unions has put out a manifesto pushing back against the spread of generative AI in game development.
## Who's behind it
The joint statement comes from the IWGB Game Workers' Branch in the UK, Game Workers Unite Ireland, Spain's CSVI and the FIOM-CGIL work council in Milan.
## What it says
The manifesto looks at generative AI from several angles: jobs and pay, the environment, ethics and the quality of the games themselves. Its central argument, according to Game Developer, is that the technology is being sold to studios as a replacement for people. The unions say that leads to job losses, unrealistic pressure on schedules and policy, and a way for employers to dodge responsibility for the results. Their main recommendation is blunt: stop using generative AI whenever possible.
The document also sets out guidelines and standards aimed at workers, studio leadership and regulators.
## Where developers stand
The unions point to GDC's 2026 State of the Game Industry survey. In it, 40 percent of professionals said they use generative AI at work, up from 36 percent the year before. But 55 percent said it's having a negative effect on the industry, 35 percent called the effect mixed, and only 8 percent saw it as positive.
Not everyone thinks the manifesto goes far enough in every direction. One developer commenting on Reddit argued it focuses mostly on threats to artists and says too little about programming jobs.

articles.title: Ghost of Yotei, Marvel's Wolverine and 007 First Light lead Grammy video game nominees
articles.dek: Five scores are up for the Grammy for best video game soundtrack, while the team behind Unbeatable says its vocal-heavy music was a poor fit for the category.
facts: Best score soundtrack for video games
Premiere ceremony, before the TV broadcast
articles.body:
The Recording Academy has named its nominees for the video game soundtrack Grammy, and Sony's first-party studios are well represented.
## The nominees
- Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora – From the Ashes, by John Paesano
- 007 First Light, by Joe Henson and Alexis Leon Smith
- Ghost of Yotei, by Toma Otowa
- Marvel's Wolverine, by David Fleming
- Star Wars Zero Company, by Gordy Haab
The winner will be named at the 69th Grammy Awards on Sunday, February 7, 2027. As in past years, the game category is handed out at the premiere ceremony a few hours before the televised show. Haab is a previous winner, having shared the award for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor.
## The vocals question
The nominations also sparked a debate about what kind of music the category rewards. RJ Lake, writer and director of rhythm game Unbeatable from D-Cell Games, said on Bluesky that the game's largely vocal soundtrack wasn't a good match for the award. After the studio submitted it for consideration, Lake said, the Grammys indicated that songs with vocals aren't what the category's voters are looking for.
According to Game Developer, that isn't a written rule, more an understanding of what the voting body expects. Lake acknowledged the game probably wouldn't have been nominated anyway. Still, the category has never nominated a soundtrack built mainly around vocal songs, which leaves a lot of game music out of the running.

articles.title: Black Friday 2026: Nintendo eShop and Xbox sales start this week
articles.dek: Nintendo's eShop sale begins today and a $499.99 Switch 2 Mario Kart World bundle follows on November 22. Xbox's sale offers up to 80% off games from tonight.
facts: $499.99 with Mario Kart World, Nov 22 – Dec 5
articles.body:
If GTA VI isn't the only thing on your list, the Black Friday console sales are starting early this year.
## Nintendo
Nintendo announced its US Black Friday offers last week, as reported by Gematsu:
- A Nintendo Switch 2 bundle with a digital copy of Mario Kart World and three months of Nintendo Switch Online for $499.99, a $50 saving. It runs from November 22 to December 5 at participating retailers, the Nintendo Store website and Nintendo's New York and San Francisco stores.
- $20 off select physical games from November 22 to 29, including Donkey Kong Bananza on Switch 2 and Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 on Switch, while supplies last.
- A Nintendo eShop and Nintendo Store sale from today, November 19, through December 2. Nintendo hasn't listed the discounted games in its announcement.
## Xbox
Microsoft has billed this as its biggest sale of the year on games and accessories. According to Gaming Route's summary of the Xbox Wire announcement, it starts at 9 PM Pacific on November 19 and runs to December 2, with up to 80 percent off more than 2,000 Xbox and PC games.
Deals named in the post reportedly include 30 percent off Gears of War: E-Day Premium Edition, 25 percent off Forza Horizon 6 Premium Edition, 55 percent off NBA 2K27 and 80 percent off Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade. Xbox Design Lab controllers are reportedly up to 15 percent off with free engraving. There's no Xbox console price cut. The offers are for the US, and other regions may differ.
We'll cover PlayStation's plans when Sony shares them.

articles.title: Xbox Game Pass adds The Outlast Trials, Hela and Arkheron in late November
articles.dek: Microsoft's second November wave brings High on Life 2, Motorslice and two day-one launches, while eight games including Aliens: Dark Descent leave on November 30.
facts: High on Life 2, The Outlast Trials
articles.body:
Microsoft has laid out the rest of November's Xbox Game Pass lineup, and it runs into early December.

articles.title: Ubisoft posts a €254.5 million half-year loss and spins out a generative AI studio
articles.dek: Net bookings fell 16.5% in the six months to September, headcount dropped by about 1,100, and Ubisoft confirmed Motherbrain as a dedicated subsidiary for AI in gameplay.
facts: Down close to 1,100 in six months
Net bookings down high single digits
articles.body:
Ubisoft's first-half results show a publisher still shrinking while it reorganizes. In the six months to September 30, net bookings came to €644.7 million, down 16.5% from €772.4 million a year earlier. The second quarter alone brought in €388.9 million, a 20.8% drop, though Ubisoft noted that was ahead of its own guidance of around €370 million.
The bottom line got worse. The IFRS net loss attributable to shareholders widened to €254.5 million from €161.3 million, and the IFRS operating loss grew to €189.2 million.
## Fewer people, smaller costs
Ubisoft says its headcount fell by close to 1,100 over the half and its fixed cost base dropped 6% to €660 million. The results arrived the same week Ubisoft announced 166 more layoffs in Montreal and Quebec City. It ended September with about €1.03 billion in cash, and says it used cash in mid-November to settle a €453 million convertible bond that holders chose to redeem early. A two-part refinancing plan is underway.
## Motherbrain becomes its own company
The report also confirms Motherbrain as a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay. CEO Yves Guillemot described it as the team behind Teammates, the experimental generative AI project Ubisoft showed in late 2025, which uses AI-driven characters that respond to players. According to VGC, it is not yet clear whether Motherbrain's work will ship as standalone products or be built into other Ubisoft games. Ubisoft says its new operating model, which began rolling out in January alongside six game cancellations, is now fully in place.
## What's next
Ubisoft kept its full-year targets: net bookings down by a high single-digit percentage, a negative non-IFRS operating margin, and free cash outflow of no more than €500 million. It expects around €250 million in third-quarter net bookings, with Rayman Legends Retold and Just Dance: Decades of Hits among this quarter's releases. Rainbow Six Tactics and the Heroes of Might and Magic III remake are slated for 2027.

articles.title: GTA VI's Japanese version tones down nudity and blood
articles.dek: Players in Japan found swimsuits in the shower, less gore and no way to turn it back up. Rockstar did not announce the changes ahead of launch.
facts: Nudity covered or cut, blood and gore reduced
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI players in Japan are getting a noticeably tamer game than the rest of the world, and many only found out once they started playing.
## What's different
According to Kotaku and VGC, which both cite footage and screenshots shared by Japanese players, nudity has been removed or covered throughout. Jason and Lucia wear swimwear in shower scenes, sex scenes and beach areas have been changed, and some scenes are reportedly cut altogether.
Violence is also dialed back. Japanese outlet GameSpark reports that blood from injured and dead characters is reduced, disappears faster, and that decapitations have been removed. Elsewhere, players can lower gore and switch off dismemberment in the settings, but the Japanese version offers no option to raise it. VGC says the changes appear to be cosmetic, and the missions themselves play out the same way.
## Warning signs before launch
Fans had suspected regional changes for weeks. Kotaku says the Japanese download was more than 1GB smaller than other regions, and the game's CERO rating in Japan left out the sexual content descriptors listed by rating boards elsewhere. Rockstar did not confirm any changes before release. Australian and New Zealand downloads are also slightly smaller, VGC notes, but there is no evidence yet that those versions are edited.
Kotaku also reports that the Japanese release carries only English voice acting with English and Japanese subtitles, while other regions offer more than a dozen languages but no Japanese text. Censoring Japanese releases is not new for the series, which has made similar edits in past entries.

articles.title: Digital Foundry doubts GTA VI could run on Switch 2
articles.dek: After testing the launch versions, Digital Foundry says a Switch 2 port looks extremely unlikely, with the game's CPU demands already pinning PS5 Pro to 30fps.
facts: PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S
articles.body:
Now that Grand Theft Auto VI is out, Digital Foundry has weighed in on one of the most persistent fan questions: could it ever come to Nintendo Switch 2? Its answer is a firm probably not.
## The CPU problem
In a video discussed by Nintendo Life, Digital Foundry says a Switch 2 version feels extremely unlikely at this stage. The core issue is the game's heavy CPU load. That bottleneck is why GTA VI runs at 30 frames per second even on PS5 Pro, a machine with far more processing power than Nintendo's hybrid.
Digital Foundry's John Linneman said that without major changes he could not see how the game would work on Switch 2.
## Series S already struggles
The weakest current version offers a hint of the challenge. Digital Foundry describes Xbox Series S performance as compromised, with frame rates often sitting in the mid to high 20s during normal play. The Series S is generally considered more capable than Switch 2 in raw CPU terms, so a Nintendo port would need deeper cuts than resolution alone.
## No plans announced
Rockstar has not announced any version beyond PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and has not dated a PC release. Earlier Rockstar games did eventually reach Nintendo hardware, but those ports arrived years after launch and on games that were far less demanding. For now, Switch 2 owners should not expect a trip to Leonida.

articles.title: Deltarune Chapter 6 is playable start to finish, and Chapter 7 work has begun
articles.dek: Toby Fox's fall newsletter says Chapter 6 is a structurally complete draft heading into localization, though some scenes still need work before full testing.
articles.body:
Deltarune creator Toby Fox has shared a fresh development update, and Chapter 6 has reached a big milestone.
## Chapter 6
In his Fall 2026 newsletter, as reported by PC Gamer and Nintendo Life, Fox says Chapter 6 now exists as a structurally complete draft that can be played from beginning to end. All of its maps, events and battles are in place, with the exception of one optional event that is still in progress.
That means the team can begin localization and some preliminary testing. Full testing has to wait, though, because Fox says several important scenes and details still need more work. He also made clear he does not intend to hurry the remaining polish.
Fox has previously said Chapter 6 is aimed at 2027, and that it will be shorter and more focused on the story's central mysteries than earlier chapters.
## Chapter 7
Development on Chapter 7, the planned final chapter, has only just started, with designers who finished their Chapter 6 work moving onto it. Fox says he read some of its events and dialogue to the team but stopped at a key moment, telling them they will need to finish more of the game before they find out what happens.
## Fan vote
The newsletter also settled a community vote: Queen won with 65% of the vote, and the prize is a silly bonus scene in Chapter 6. Fox says the next update should arrive once Chapter 6's localization is done.

articles.title: Ocarina of Time stays No. 1 in Japan as Metaphor: ReFantazio debuts on Switch 2
articles.dek: The Switch 2 Zelda remake sold another 86,097 boxed copies in Japan in its second full week, while Switch 2 outsold every other console combined.
articles.body:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time held the top spot in Japan's physical charts for the week of November 9 to 15, according to Famitsu data reported by Gematsu. The Switch 2 game sold 86,097 boxed copies, bringing its total to 623,138 since its November 5 launch.
## Top five
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2): 86,097
- Metaphor: ReFantazio (Switch 2, new): 11,167
- Nintendo Switch Sports Resort (Switch 2): 11,086
- Rhythm Heaven Groove (Switch): 7,779
- Minecraft Dungeons II (Switch, new): 4,264
Atlus's fantasy RPG Metaphor: ReFantazio arrived on Switch 2 in second place, narrowly ahead of Switch Sports Resort. Pikmin 4's Switch 2 Edition with Dandori Academy also debuted, at No. 8 with 2,854 copies. Final Fantasy Resonance was the only non-Nintendo-platform game in the top 10, at No. 10 on PS5.
## Hardware
Switch 2 sold 42,402 units for the week, lifting its Japanese total past 6.6 million. That was nearly three times the combined total of every other system. The PS5 family sold 11,136, almost all of it the Digital Edition, while the original Switch family sold 3,754 and Xbox Series consoles sold 707.
These figures cover only physical retail sales in Japan and do not include digital downloads. GTA VI's November 19 launch will fall in next week's data.

articles.title: Rockstar puts GTA VI's day-one retail sales at $3.79 billion
articles.dek: Take-Two's own estimate, filed with US regulators, calls it the biggest entertainment launch ever and adds a record 32.5 million units sold before release.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive have put their own number on Grand Theft Auto VI's opening: an estimated $3.79 billion in worldwide retail sales on day one. The figure appeared in a press release dated November 20 that Take-Two also filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission as part of an 8-K report.
The release calls GTA VI the biggest entertainment launch in history and says it set a sales record for entertainment in any medium. It also says the game sold 32.5 million units before release, which Rockstar describes as a record across all platforms.
## How the number was counted
A footnote says the $3.79 billion is based on company estimates through the end of November 19 worldwide. The release does not split digital from physical sales or say how units are defined, so it is not directly comparable with Take-Two's quarterly net bookings, which use a different accounting basis.
The official figure is well above outside estimates published the same week. Sensor Tower had estimated about $2.36 billion and 24.6 million copies by the end of launch day, and earlier reports had put preorder revenue below $2 billion.
## What else Rockstar said
The release highlights the game's 99 Metacritic score and lists the stores carrying it: the PlayStation Store, Microsoft Store, Rockstar Games Store and retailers worldwide. GTA VI is out on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with no PC version announced.
Rockstar president Sam Houser said the studio was "incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world." For context, the release notes that GTA V has sold in nearly 235 million units and the series nearly 480 million.
Take-Two reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 net bookings forecast of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion earlier in November.

articles.title: GTA VI's Metacritic user score sinks to 5.6 as fans start review-bombing Zelda
articles.dek: Thousands of zero scores have hit GTA VI's user page, and some GTA fans have retaliated against Ocarina of Time, which held Metacritic's top user score.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI may be the best-reviewed game on Metacritic, but its user score tells a different story. According to VGC, the game's user rating had fallen to 5.6 out of 10 from more than 10,000 reviews as of November 23, against a critic score of 99.
Metacritic held back user reviews until 36 hours after launch, its usual practice, after removing fake reviews that had been posted before the game was out. Once the page opened, a large share of the scores were zeros.
## What the low scores say
VGC reports that many of the zero-score reviews complain about the game's story, describing it as a relationship simulator built around keeping co-lead Lucia happy. Others use culture-war language to attack the game. VGC called the pattern of zero scores suspicious.
## The retaliation
Some GTA fans have responded by targeting other games at the top of Metacritic's charts. The 2026 Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which had the highest user score on the site, has received a wave of zero ratings over the past few days. Several reviewers say they are GTA fans who believe Zelda fans bombed GTA VI first.
The remake's user score was still 8.3 when VGC checked, propped up by tens of thousands of positive reviews posted after its launch. The original 1998 Ocarina of Time and SoulCalibur, third on the all-time list, have also picked up zero scores from GTA fans.
## Why it matters
User scores on Metacritic tend to cluster at zero and ten, and coordinated campaigns have pushed games up and down the lists before. The swings say more about fan rivalries than about how good any of these games are. Critic scores for both GTA VI and Ocarina of Time are unaffected.

articles.title: GTA VI gets its first post-launch patch, with no patch notes
articles.dek: Update 1.002.002 is rolling out in stages on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar hasn't said what it changes.
facts: About 604MB on PS5, 1.6GB on Xbox Series X|S
articles.body:
Rockstar has started rolling out the first Grand Theft Auto VI update since the game launched on November 19. Version 1.002.002 on PS5, listed as 1.0.2.2 on Xbox Series X|S, began reaching players on November 23.
According to Push Square and Tbreak, the download is about 604MB on PS5 and 1.6GB on Xbox Series X|S. It is the third patch in roughly ten days, following two pre-launch updates on November 13 and November 16.
## A staggered release
The update is not arriving for everyone at once. Rockstar dataminer Tex2 reported that it would reach a third of PS5 owners first, two thirds after about three hours and everyone within six hours. Push Square says the staging appears designed to avoid overloading servers. Players who don't see it yet can check for updates manually from the game's options menu on console.
## What it fixes
Rockstar has not published patch notes, and neither of the earlier updates came with any. That leaves players guessing. Some reports describe the game feeling smoother after the update, but there is no confirmation of performance changes, and Tbreak cautions that this may be a placebo effect. The game's 30fps target on consoles, including PS5 Pro, is unchanged as far as anyone knows.
Players have reported a handful of launch bugs, including a PS5 error code and an Xbox glitch that runs gameplay at double speed. It is not known whether this patch addresses either.

articles.title: Hacker group Cyberleek claims to be leaking a GTA VI development build
articles.dek: The group says it has released every file from a November Xbox build except the executable, which it is holding back on a countdown. Rockstar hasn't commented.
facts: Main executable, so the files can't be run
Take-Two has subpoenaed Discord over earlier leaks
articles.body:
A hacker group calling itself Cyberleek says it has begun releasing a development build of Grand Theft Auto VI, VGC reports. The claim surfaced on November 19, the day the game launched, and has not been confirmed by Rockstar or Take-Two.
The group's site lists a download labeled as an Xbox build, version 1.0.2.1, dated November 2026. Cyberleek says it is distributing every file by torrent except the main executable, which it says is being held back on a countdown. It has also said it could release the executable sooner if a crypto token it promotes reaches a certain value, and that a PS5 build would follow only as a fallback.
## What we know
Screenshots shared on social media appear to show files from an Xbox development build, according to VGC. Without the executable, nobody can actually run the build, and the files' authenticity has not been independently verified.
Cyberleek has spent months posting what it says is GTA VI gameplay and frames its campaign as a protest over consumer rights, including the lack of a traditional disc release. VGC reports that the group has pushed crypto donations and required them to vote in polls on what to leak next.
## Rockstar's position
Rockstar has not commented on the claimed build. Take-Two has previously described its investigation into GTA VI leaks as rapidly evolving and has filed subpoenas asking Discord for information on specific servers and users.
The claim comes days after Arion Kurtaj, the hacker behind the 2022 GTA VI leak, pleaded guilty in a separate case. Players should be wary of any download claiming to be a leaked build: unofficial files from anonymous sources are a common way to spread malware.

articles.title: Expedition 33's former lead writer backs the Rockstar union push
articles.dek: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen says layoff fears at Rockstar after GTA VI's record launch show developers don't share fairly in the value they create.
facts: Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, former lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
articles.body:
The former lead writer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has weighed in on the union drive at Rockstar Games, arguing that worries about layoffs after Grand Theft Auto VI's record launch point to a deeper imbalance in the industry.
In comments reported by PC Gamer, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen said the people who create the value in games like GTA VI don't receive a proportionate share of it. She said she hopes the Rockstar team succeeds in unionizing. Svedberg-Yen left Expedition 33 developer Sandfall Interactive in July.
## The backdrop
Her comments follow an op-ed in The Guardian by Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte, who wrote that there was no sign layoffs were coming but that colleagues were still anxious about their jobs. Big studios have often cut staff after a major release as they shift to post-launch support, and the past few years have seen tens of thousands of job losses across the industry.
Rockstar's UK staff are voting on union recognition, with the ballot closing on November 26. The union says about 1,600 staff are eligible to vote.
## Why her voice carries weight
Expedition 33 was one of the breakout hits of 2025, made by a small team, and Svedberg-Yen has become a prominent voice on how developers are treated and credited. Her intervention adds to a growing list of developers outside Rockstar publicly backing the vote, as GTA VI's sales figures make the gap between a game's earnings and job security for its makers hard to ignore.
